chapter_title: Case Studies C — Nemotron, Distillation SFT
course_outline_concepts: Nemotron-4 340B + Nemotron-Ultra: >98% synthetic SFT + 5-dim HelpSteer2 preference
R1-distill: what data DeepSeek generated and how it was SFT-consumed
Bespoke-Stratos ~17K trace curation: contamination checks, the 'cheap frontier reasoning' recipe
Sky-T1 $450 run — what they pulled from R1 and what they filtered out
When distillation SFT is enough vs when you still need RL (s1/LIMO vs full R1)

sources.what_to_extract: Nemotron-4 synthetic alignment pipeline: >98% synthetic SFT/DPO/RPO, ~20K human anchor, category-seeded prompt generator, RM-as-filter; ~800K code SFT + 200K general SFT + 160K DPO + 300K RPO; Genetic Instruct for code.

Nemotron-4-340B-Reward: 5-attribute regression head (helpfulness, correctness, coherence, complexity, verbosity); HelpSteer2 10K human preferences; per-attribute L2 loss; weighted-sum aggregation for RL use; self-bootstrapping synthetic pipeline; 9T pretraining tokens.

Nemotron 3 Nano/Super/Ultra family: multi-environment RL as successor to Nemotron-4 sequential RLHF; GenRM open release; reasoning budget control; 3.2B active / 31.6B total MoE Nano; Nemotron-4 template carried forward but hyperparameter opacity.

R1 pipeline: cold-start SFT -> Reasoning RL (GRPO, LR 3e-6, KL 0.001, eps=10, G=16, 32k tokens) -> rejection-sampling SFT produces 800K (600K reasoning + 200K non-reasoning) -> alignment RL; distillation into Qwen/Llama students is pure SFT, no RL.
R1 model-report specifics: six distilled checkpoints (1.5B/7B/8B/14B/32B/70B); 800K figure from README; AIME24 79.8% R1 vs o1 79.2%; MATH500 97.3%; R1-Zero aha moment.

R1-0528 refresh: same V3 base + more post-training compute; R1-Distill family SFT-only on Llama-3.1 8B/70B + Llama-3.3 70B + Qwen-2.5 1.5B/7B/14B/32B; distillation-only is competitive with full RL for reasoning transfer.
Public DeepSeek doc says Qwen-based distills use 800K samples curated with DeepSeek-R1; per-source breakdown is not disclosed; student trained with pure SFT; format-preservation is load-bearing.

17K curated (prompt, R1-trace) pairs; ~$800 API cost + ~$4K training; 7K math + 5K code + 5K science seed pool; SymPy + unit-test + GPT-4o judge; ~30-50% reject rate; AIME24 ~63% / MATH500 ~93% / LCB ~57% within 2-3 pts of R1-Distill-Qwen-32B.

$450 Sky-T1-32B-Preview: QwQ-32B-preview teacher (local vLLM), 17K traces, 3 epochs x 19 hours on 8xH100, LR 1e-5, seq 32K, BF16 + FSDP via Llama-Factory; GPT-4o rewriter cleanup +4 AIME; MATH500 82.4%, AIME24 43.3%, LCB-Easy 86.3%, GPQA-Dia 56.8%.

OpenR1-Math-220k: 220K problems x 2 R1 traces = 440K total; Math-Verify SymPy-based; ~20% reject rate; OpenR1-Qwen-7B MATH~80% AIME24~40%; GRPO on top adds +3-5 AIME pts -- the chapter's only in-table hard evidence that SFT alone is not the ceiling.

s1K: 1000 curated question-trace pairs from 59K candidate pool; Gemini traces, 26 min on 16 H100 FSDP SFT on Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct; budget-forcing at inference (append 'Wait' to suppress early stop); AIME24 56.7%, MATH500 93.0%, GPQA-Dia 59.6%.

LIMO: 817 hand-curated long-CoT samples on Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct base; Less-is-More Reasoning Hypothesis — base model must already contain the domain knowledge, small high-quality demos elicit; AIME24 63.3% MATH500 95.6% using 1% of prior data.

OpenThoughts3 1.2M: systematic recipe search (1000+ ablations); QwQ-32B beats R1 as teacher for Qwen2.5-7B even though R1 scores higher; no answer-side filter beats keep-everything; exact dedup for math, no dedup for code.
